physics_goals.quote: The BRAHMS experiment was designed to measure charged hadrons over a wide range of rapidity and transverse momentum
physics_goals.value: Measure charged hadrons over a wide range of rapidity and transverse momentum to study the reaction mechanisms of relativistic heavy-ion reactions and the properties of the excited nuclear matter formed

summary.plain: BRAHMS was one of the four original experiments at Brookhaven's RHIC collider. Its two movable spectrometers measured charged particles over a very wide range of angles in gold-gold and other collisions, from the first RHIC run in 2000 until June 2006.
summary.technical: Broad RAnge Hadron Magnetic Spectrometers: movable forward and mid-rapidity spectrometers measuring identified charged hadrons over a wide range of rapidity and transverse momentum in Au+Au, d+Au and p+p collisions at RHIC (2000-2006); reported nuclear modification factors falling with rapidity in d+Au and a 2005 white-paper assessment of the evidence for the quark-gluon plasma and the colour glass condensate.
